# BrightSpring Health Services Congratulates StepStone Family & Youth Services on 2026 Angels in Adoption Honor


September 30, 2026


BrightSpring Health Services congratulates[StepStone Family & Youth Services](https://www.stepstoneyouth.com/) on being named a ***2026 Angels in Adoption*** honoree by the[Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute (CCAI)](https://www.ccainstitute.org/) . This recognition highlights StepStone’s dedication to helping children in foster care find safe, stable, and permanent families.


StepStone Vice President Jennifer Parks and BrightSpring Vice President of Service Excellence and Stakeholder Relations Chris Hempfling accepted the award on behalf of StepStone on September 29 at the *Angels in Adoption Leadership Program* in Washington, D.C. CCAI and Kentucky Congressman Morgan McGarvey presented them with a commemorative pin, certificate, and letter of acknowledgment.


Congressman McGarvey nominated StepStone for this distinction, recognizing the organization’s exceptional work. StepStone was selected for its nine-state foster care network and its focus on the following priorities:


- **Family preservation** , supporting families in remaining together whenever it is safe to do so
- **Kinship care** , connecting children with relatives who already know and love them
- **Trauma-informed support** , addressing the needs of children and caregivers with an understanding of their experiences
- **Permanency** , working toward lasting family connections rather than temporary placements


Each year, CCAI selects individuals, families, and organizations across the country that have demonstrated a commitment to improving the lives of children in need of permanent, safe, and nurturing homes. Through its Angels in Adoption Leadership Program, CCAI honors those who have made extraordinary contributions to adoption, permanency, and child welfare. The program also provides Members of Congress with greater visibility into foster care and adoption efforts in their states and communities.


---


**About Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute (CCAI)**


Founded in 2001, the **[Congressional Coalition on Adoption Institute (CCAI)](https://www.ccainstitute.org/)** is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization dedicated to raising awareness about the millions of children around the world in need of safe and nurturing families and to eliminating the barriers that hinder these children from realizing their basic right to a family. The creation of CCAI sought to match the commitment of Members of Congress’ Adoption Caucus, the Congressional Coalition on Adoption, with the information and resources needed to make the dream of a family a reality for every child.


Although the Adoption Caucus (CCA) and CCAI are distinct entities, they are closely linked in partnership. Over 135 Members of the 119th Congress have joined and are actively engaged in supporting legislation and policy that improves the lives of children and families in the United States and around the world. Both the CCA and CCAI are deeply committed to bipartisanship, strengthening families, and permanency. When Members of Congress hear direct experiences of those affected by child welfare systems, they become engaged in this issue and work to bring about legislative improvements to ensure each child’s right to a family is realized. As a convener, CCAI brings together voices of experience and expertise to the U.S. Congress.


**About the Angels in Adoption® Program**


CCAI’s **[Angels in Adoption® Leadership Program](https://www.ccainstitute.org/congress-engage/angels/angels-in-adoption-congress)** honors a wide spectrum of individuals, couples, and organizations making extraordinary contributions to adoption, foster care, permanency, and child welfare. Once selected, Angel honorees are invited to travel to Washington, D.C. for a leadership program to participate in congressional meetings with federal policymakers, receive advocacy and educational training, meet with fellow advocates, and receive recognition at the Angels Celebration held in their honor. These amazing honorees (like you!) represent the wide spectrum of individuals involved in child welfare who are making a difference. Since the program’s inception in 1999, more than 3,200 Angels have received this honor. You can learn more about CCAI and the Angels program on our website.
